summary:
We created Operation Ducks, an interactive map that is intended to help farmers use NASA Earth observation data to answer practical questions about a plot of land. Users can draw a field boundary on the map and explore NASA Worldview satellite imagery, NASA POWER weather records, and available soil and crop history of that plot. To keep things user friendly, you can also ask Duck, our voice assistant, questions such as "What could I plant here?" or "which plants grow best here?" to get recommendations from our custom trained AI. 

Operation Ducks addresses the important challenge by giving the world’s food producers information on new plots of land or evaluates the health of a field in use. This technology will keep farmers informed in a time of shifting temperatures so they can make the best possible choices. Duck Ai takes the past 45 years of data into account while evaluating to ensure you have the highest chance to get a good harvest.
details:
Operation Ducks is an interactive map that helps growers and students use satellite and weather data to understand conditions on a farm field. Users can search for a location, draw a field boundary, and explore available imagery, temperature, rainfall, soil data, and crop history.

Duck, our assistant, uses the same field selection as the map. Users can ask by text or voice, “What crop rotation options make sense here?” Duck uses the field’s location and available records to summarize conditions, suggest options, and link to supporting sources when available. Bringing these records together helps growers compare options and decide what to investigate on the ground.

We built the app with TypeScript, React, Next.js, and MapLibre GL. We used Python for Duck’s backend, PyTorch for model development, and Jupyter notebooks for training and evaluation. Our data sources include NASA POWER weather records and NASA Worldview imagery.

Our team considered cloud cover, gaps in crop records, the age of observations, and the area each observation covers. A regional rainfall estimate, for example, provides context, while conditions can vary across a field. These limits shaped how we present sources and explain what the data can support.
